test_overview: Evaluated the search-with-threads test plan (8 steps, max 66 points) against the Team Chat SPA at http://localhost:8000 (context_A, logged in as alice). Login and landing on #general succeeded. Step 1 (test_create_searchable_thread_in_general) FAILED fatally with multiple defects in core message/thread handling: (1) The first Send of "Search test ALPHA root message." did not post on the initial click; after a subsequent click it posted, but #general then rendered the SAME message 12 times in the timeline (12 rows, all data-testid="message-1", identical author/time/content) — a visible duplicate-rendering bug associated with the 2s pollNewMessages re-render. (2) The message's "Reply in thread" per-message action did NOT open the thread view on the first click — the click landed (button [active]) but the view remained "#general"; only a second click opened "Thread in #general", consistent with the poll re-render reverting the first navigation. (3) Most critically, thread replies cannot be posted at all: with the draft "Thread reply ALPHA-1 in general." in the composer, Send was clicked twice and Enter (the app's supported send shortcut) was pressed once; the reply never appeared, the draft never cleared, no composer error was shown, and the thread kept displaying "No replies yet. Reply to start the thread." Therefore the required replies (ALPHA-1/ALPHA-2) were never created and the thread could not be properly populated/navigated. Because every subsequent step (2–8) depends on searchable thread replies from #general (ALPHA) and the DM (BETA), and the app's thread-reply send is non-functional, the fatal failure in step 1 blocked all remaining steps. Awarded 0/66.

steps.description: test_create_searchable_thread_in_general: FAILED (fatal). Login+land on #general OK, but: root message initially did not post then rendered 12x duplicated; first 'Reply in thread' click reverted (thread view only opened on second click); thread replies could not be posted via Send (x2) or Enter — draft never cleared, 'No replies yet' persisted. Required thread replies ALPHA-1/ALPHA-2 were never created, blocking all dependent steps.
